profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Tyler Technologies | Georgia Tech CS | Full-Stack Development
profile.summary:
I'm a Software Engineer at Tyler Technologies and a Computer Science graduate from the Georgia Institute of Technology, with approximately two years of professional experience in enterprise software development.
Previously, at Hyundai Glovis, I worked on developing, maintaining, and improving enterprise applications supporting large-scale automotive logistics operations. My experience includes backend development with Java and Spring Boot, database optimization using SQL, and building Python-based automation and data-processing tools to improve operational efficiency.
I've also worked across frontend and backend systems, troubleshot production issues, and collaborated with cross-functional teams on cloud modernization and system integration initiatives involving AWS and Siemens technologies.
My technical background includes Java, Python, C#, SQL, Spring Boot, and web development, with a strong interest in software architecture, system reliability, and scalable application development.
As I begin my next chapter at Tyler Technologies, I'm excited to continue growing as a software engineer, contribute to meaningful software solutions, and take on new technical challenges.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Software Engineer at Tyler Technologies, a company specializing in software solutions for the public sector.

Focused on contributing to software development, collaborating with engineering teams, and building reliable, maintainable applications.
positions.insights: Software Engineering Practices, Software Development and +3 skills

positions.title: Software Developer Senior IT Specialist
positions.description:
- Enhanced multiple core screens and backend workflows in IVELES, a mission‑critical Spring Boot web application supporting daily VPC logistics operations.
- Improved SQL query performance by 20–30% through refactoring legacy logic and optimizing data access patterns.
- Delivered new backend features and UI/UX improvements that increased system reliability and supported high‑volume vehicle processing workflows.
- Built a Python‑based web crawler to extract operational metrics from the LMO dashboard, enabling automated monitoring without backend integration.
- Developed an alerting system that sends real‑time notifications via SMS and email, reducing manual dashboard monitoring time by 70–80%.
- Collaborated with AWS solution architects to explore cloud modernization patterns using S3, Athena, Glue, and related analytics services.
- Served as the technical lead representing Hyundai Glovis in a joint Siemens/AWS initiative, driving early‑stage architecture planning and feasibility discussions for Mendix‑based operational visibility solutions.
- Acted as the primary technical point of contact between Glovis, Siemens engineers, and AWS architects to align requirements and technical direction.

projects.title: Automated Data Monitoring & Alert System
projects.description:
Independently developed a Python-based monitoring and alert system to automate operational data collection and notification workflows in an enterprise logistics environment.
- Solely developed and implemented the monitoring system, including data collection, processing, and automated notifications.
- Built a Python-based web scraping pipeline to periodically retrieve and monitor operational data.
- Implemented automated SMS and email notifications to deliver timely updates when relevant conditions were detected.
- Developed structured CSV-based data processing and logging to support tracking and analysis.

Packaged the application for execution in a dedicated operational environment, reducing the need for repetitive manual monitoring.

Technologies: Python, Web Scraping, Data Processing, CSV, SMS/Email Automation

projects.title: Google GeoGuesser (ChromeOS Collaboration)
projects.description: Developed a ChromeOS-native GeoGuesser game using JavaScript, TypeScript, Webpack, LIT, and Google Streetview API. Collaborated with Google ChromeOS product and engineering teams as the front-end developer in a 5‑person team.
